title: Untested artifacts rot silently: 6 of 8 shipped configs and the TS E2E suite were broken for months
content: Two 1.3.2 follow-ups found long-standing breakage only because something finally exercised it. (1) phase12: a one-line test that loads every file under config/ as ServerConfig showed 6 of 8 shipped configs, production and the documented example included, rejected at startup by any parser: eviction_policy "lru" (never valid; the enum has used "allkeys-lru" since at least 0.13), seeds/master_address given as hostnames to SocketAddr fields, and required queue/rate_limit sections missing. Nobody noticed because no code path loads the examples. Keep every_shipped_config_loads, and when swapping a parser, diff old vs new on every shipped file at the serde_json::Value level, then probe YAML 1.1 edge cases (yes/no/on/off, 0755, 1_000, ~/null into String) on typed targets; serde-saphyr differed only on those. (2) phase13: the TS E2E suite (RUN_E2E) had not run since 1.0.0 (config path moved). Once fixed, 9/22 failed, and every native failure was a reply shape the SDK passed through untranslated (bare arrays vs {queues}/{rooms}, positional RESP3 QCONSUME, flat QSTATS pairs, JSON-text EVAL results, "OK" for ack) plus two binary-encoding bugs (number[] payload stringified; RESP3 transport String()-ing Uint8Array). The fastest diagnosis was a 20-line probe printing getClient().sendCommand() raw replies against a live release server on each transport; then a unit test per reply shape. Gated suites need a scheduled run or they rot.
